families.label: Visuomotor rotation
families.about: Each line is one group of participants who reached to targets while the cursor was rotated by the same amount on the same schedule. Hand angles are flipped so that moving against the rotation is positive; 100% means the hand fully cancels the rotation.

measures.label: Early adaptation
measures.text: mean of feedback trials 2 to 11 of the first rotation block, minus the participant's baseline

measures.label: Late adaptation
measures.text: mean of the last 20 feedback trials of the first rotation block, minus the participant's baseline

measures.label: Aftereffect, told to stop aiming
measures.text: mean of the first 10 no-feedback trials right after the block, when such trials follow it; told to stop aiming and reach straight to the target

measures.label: Aftereffect, told to keep aiming
measures.text: mean of the first 10 no-feedback trials right after the block, when such trials follow it; told to keep aiming as during the block

measures.label: Aftereffect, no instruction recorded
measures.text: mean of the first 10 no-feedback trials right after the block, when such trials follow it; no instruction recorded for these trials

measures.label: Trials to half
measures.text: rotation trials until the group mean (5-trial moving average) first reaches half of its late value; only for groups that learned clearly

families.label: Error clamp
families.about: Each line is one group of participants who saw a cursor that always moved at a fixed angle from the target, whatever their hand did, and were told to ignore it. Hand angles are flipped so that moving away from the clamp (implicit adaptation) is positive. Clamp sizes differ between studies; the size filter keeps one range.

measures.label: Early adaptation
measures.text: mean of feedback trials 2 to 11 of the first clamp block, minus the participant's baseline

measures.label: Late adaptation
measures.text: mean of the last 20 feedback trials of the first clamp block, minus the participant's baseline

measures.label: Aftereffect, told to stop aiming
measures.text: mean of the first 10 no-feedback trials right after the block, when such trials follow it; told to stop aiming and reach straight to the target

measures.label: Aftereffect, aiming forbidden
measures.text: mean of the first 10 no-feedback trials right after the block, when such trials follow it; told not to aim (for example, to keep ignoring the cursor)

measures.label: Aftereffect, no instruction recorded
measures.text: mean of the first 10 no-feedback trials right after the block, when such trials follow it; no instruction recorded for these trials

measures.label: Trials to half
measures.text: clamp trials until the group mean (5-trial moving average) first reaches half of its late value; only for groups that learned clearly

families.label: Split-belt walking
families.about: Each line is one group who walked on a treadmill whose two belts were split to different speeds. y is step length asymmetry minus the person's own baseline: it drops when the belts split and climbs back toward 0 as people adapt.

cmp.value: Step length asymmetry column, (fast - slow) / (fast + slow)
cmp.note: y is your asymmetry minus each person's mean over their last 50 baseline strides.

measures.label: Initial perturbation
measures.text: mean of strides 1 to 5 of the first split block

measures.label: Early adaptation
measures.text: mean of strides 6 to 30 of the split block

measures.label: Late adaptation
measures.text: mean of the last 30 strides of the split block

measures.label: Aftereffect
measures.text: mean of the first 5 tied-belt treadmill strides right after the split block (a catch counts)

families.methods: Split-belt walking: step length asymmetry, (fast - slow) / (fast + slow) step length, per stride, minus each person's mean over 50 tied treadmill strides on the same slope before the split, leaving out the last 5. Splits that ramp up, are walked on a slope, or show step-length targets on screen are listed but not pooled.

families.label: Saccade adaptation
families.about: Each line is one group who made saccades to a target that stepped during the saccade, by the same amount and in the same direction on every trial. y is the change in saccade gain from baseline, signed so that adapting toward the step is positive (a gain decrease for a backward step).

cmp.note: y is the gain change from each person's baseline mean, times 100, positive toward the step.

measures.label: Early adaptation
measures.text: mean of trials 2 to 11 of the first step block

measures.label: Late adaptation
measures.text: mean of the last 20 trials of the step block

measures.label: Aftereffect
measures.text: mean of the first 10 trials right after the block, when the target no longer stepped

families.methods: Saccade adaptation: gain is the primary saccade amplitude along the target direction divided by the target distance; y is its change from the person's baseline mean, in % of the target distance, positive toward the step. % of the step divides that by the step size.

families.label: Force field reaching
families.about: Each line is one group who reached while a robot pushed the hand sideways in proportion to its speed (a velocity-dependent curl field). y is force compensation on channel trials, the share of the field's force the person pushed against the channel wall; 100% means full compensation.

cmp.value: Force compensation column (%, empty on non-channel trials)
cmp.note: Values are used as they are, in % of the field.

measures.label: Early adaptation
measures.text: mean of the channel trials among the first 40 trials of the first field block

measures.label: Late adaptation
measures.text: mean of the last 5 channel trials of the field block

measures.label: Aftereffect
measures.text: mean of the first 5 channel trials right after the field block, when channel trials follow it

families.methods: Force field: force compensation on channel trials, the force pushed into the channel wall as a % of the force the field would have applied (no baseline subtraction). Field trials have no value, so gaps of up to 12 trials are bridged in the pooled mean. Ramped fields, opposing fields switched by context, and studies with only kinematic errors are listed but not pooled.

families.label: Sequence learning (SRT)
families.lineWord: practised the same sequence on the same schedule
families.about: Each line is one group who pressed keys in answer to cues that followed one repeating sequence, block after block. y is how much faster they answered than in their first sequence block; a random or new-sequence block right after training shows how much of the speed-up belonged to the sequence.
families.unitName: ms faster than the first sequence block
families.x: Blocks from the first sequence block

measures.label: Early speed-up
measures.text: mean speed-up in sequence blocks 2 and 3

measures.label: Overall speed-up
measures.text: speed-up in the last sequence block (general and sequence-specific learning together)

measures.label: Sequence-specific learning
measures.text: RT in the random or new-sequence block right after training minus RT in the last sequence block

families.methods: Sequence learning: per block, the mean RT of correct key presses the authors kept (a 3-SD rule per person when they marked none, warm-up presses left out), and y is the first sequence block's mean minus this block's, in ms. Alternating (ASRT) and probabilistic sequences, and designs with no random block after training, are listed but not pooled.

cmp.value: Mean reaction time column (ms), one row per block
cmp.note: One row per block: y is the first sequence block's RT minus each block's RT.

families.label: Speech formant adaptation
families.about: Each line is one group who heard their own voice through headphones with the vowel formants shifted on every trial of a block. y is how much they changed their produced formants against the shift, in % of the full shift; 100% means the shift is fully cancelled.

cmp.value: Produced formant column (the shifted formant, in the unit of the shift)
cmp.note: y is minus the change from each person's baseline mean, in % of the shift (one formant, one baseline for all words).

measures.label: Early adaptation
measures.text: mean of the first 10 trials at the full shift

measures.label: Late adaptation
measures.text: mean of the last 30 trials at the full shift

measures.label: Aftereffect
measures.text: mean of the first 10 trials with normal feedback right after the shift ends

families.methods: Speech: the produced formant change from each person's baseline for the same word, projected on the direction of the shift and flipped, in % of the full shift. Ramp trials are drawn but early and late use only trials at the full shift.

onset_first_trial.Gastrock2020_SciRep: the file starts at the rotated training: the aligned session is not in the deposit (conversion notes: 'Aligned-session and top-up training trials are not in the deposit')
onset_first_trial.Ruttle2016_PLoSONE: the file starts at the rotated training: the aligned baseline (270 trials on day 1) is not in the deposit (conversion notes)
onset_first_trial.Modchalingam2023_SciRep: the file starts at the rotated training: the aligned baseline block (66 cursor and 18 no-cursor reaches) is not in the deposit (conversion notes)
onset_first_trial.Kobayashi2024_eLife: each sequence starts at the rotation onset after 360 veridical baseline reaches that the deposit does not encode (conversion notes)
onset_first_trial.Avraham2022_eLife: the design has no baseline: the clamp starts on the first trial (conversion notes: 'No baseline')
